title: Save/Load World Snapshots
description:
Persist and restore world configurations.

Snapshot contains:
- World name, version
- All node configs (type, position, parameters)
- Environment settings (gravity, tick rate)
- Passive element positions and properties
- Does NOT save active tokenes (ephemeral, regenerated by running emitters)

Storage:
- JSON serialization (human-readable, diffable)
- Store in priv/worlds/ for bundled examples
- Store in ~/.quantok/worlds/ for user saves
- Or use Ecto + SQLite for structured storage (decide later)

UI:
- Save button -> name prompt -> persist
- Load button -> file picker / list of saved worlds
- Auto-save option (periodic)
- Example worlds bundled: 'hello world', 'date pipeline', 'echo chain'

Format versioning: include schema version for forward compat.
close_reason: Snapshot module with JSON serialization/deserialization, save/load from files, version checking. 2 bundled example worlds (hello_world, date_pipeline). Save/Load UI in sidebar with world list. clear_nodes client event. 7 new tests.

title: Emitter -> Tokene Pipeline (First Demo)
description:
Wire up the full emitter -> falling tokenes flow. This is the first working demo.

Flow:
1. User creates a ShellEmitter node (e.g., command: 'date', chunker: word)
2. User triggers emit (button or auto)
3. Server executes command, chunks output via selected chunker
4. Server creates Tokene structs, publishes {:emit, emitter_id, [tokene]} events
5. Client receives events, spawns Rapier rigid bodies + Three.js meshes at emitter position
6. Tokenes fall due to gravity
7. Tokenes land on floor (or fall off screen and get cleaned up)

This validates the full stack: Elixir command execution -> chunking -> event push -> client physics -> rendering.

Milestone: see 'Fri Mar 6 ...' tokens literally falling from an emitter box.
close_reason: Full pipeline wired: sidebar button fires emitter → World.fire_emitter → Shell.run → Chunker.chunk → PubSub {:emit} → LiveView push_event → world_hook spawns Rapier bodies + Three.js meshes → tokenes fall with gravity → floor collision → offscreen cleanup. Server returns 200 on /world.

title: Passive World Elements
description:
Implement passive/static elements that shape the physical world.

Elements:
1. Floor - horizontal static collider, configurable width and position
2. Wall - vertical static collider
3. Ramp - angled static collider, configurable angle
4. Funnel - V-shaped pair of angled surfaces, guides tokenes to a point
5. Attractor - applies force toward its center on nearby tokenes (inverse square or configurable falloff)
6. Repeller - applies force away from center on nearby tokenes

Physics properties:
- Friction coefficient (configurable per surface)
- Bounciness/restitution
- Attractors/repellers have configurable strength and radius

These are essential for building interesting setups - funneling tokenes from emitter to collector, creating paths, etc.
close_reason: Passive spawn UI (ramp/wall/funnel buttons), spawns static physics bodies with angle/friction/restitution config, renders with appropriate styling. Floor already exists as default.

title: Node Behaviour & Types
description:
Define the Node behaviour and implement Emitter, Collector, Transformer, and Passive node types.

Node behaviour:
- Common fields: id, position, type, label
- tick/2 callback for per-tick logic

Emitter nodes:
- ShellEmitter: runs a shell command, chunks stdout
- Fields: command, chunker, emit_rate, auto_repeat
- On fire: executes command, chunks output, emits tokenes

Collector nodes:
- ShellCollector: buffers input, runs command with collected text
- DisplayCollector: just shows collected text
- Fields: buffer_capacity, buffer_contents, trigger_mode (:on_full | :manual | :on_tick)
- Buffer is a visible ordered list of slots

Transformer nodes:
- Splitter: breaks tokenes down one encoding level
- Crusher: breaks tokenes all the way to bytes
- Fuser: combines adjacent tokenes in proximity into one
- Retokenizer: re-chunks using a different chunker
- Heater: reduces integrity of nearby tokenes
- Cooler: increases integrity
- Painter: tags tokenes with color/metadata
- Filter: only passes tokenes matching a pattern
- Duplicator: copies tokenes passing through

Passive nodes:
- Floor: static collision surface
- Wall: vertical barrier
- Funnel: guides tokenes toward a point
- Attractor: gravity well
- Repeller: pushes tokenes away
- Ramp: angled surface
close_reason: Node behaviour + Emitter (shell, manual), Collector (echo, shell), Transformer (splitter, crusher, heater, cooler, filter, duplicator, painter), Passive (floor, wall, ramp, funnel, attractor, repeller). 95 tests passing.

title: Chunker Behaviour & Implementations
description:
Define the Chunker behaviour and implement all chunking strategies.

Behaviour:
  @callback chunk(binary()) :: [binary()]
  @callback encoding() :: atom()

Implementations:
- BitChunker - split into individual bits
- ByteChunker - split into individual bytes
- RuneChunker - split on grapheme clusters (String.graphemes)
- WordChunker - split on configurable delimiter (default space)
- NgramChunker(n) - sliding window of n characters
- SentenceChunker - split on sentence boundaries
- PhraseChunker - split on phrase boundaries (commas, semicolons, etc)
- BPEChunker - tiktoken-compatible BPE tokenizer (see quantok-3)

Each chunker should be well-tested with property-based tests where appropriate.
close_reason: All 8 chunker implementations done: bit, byte, rune, word, ngram, phrase, sentence, BPE. Tests passing.

title: Additional Collector Types
description:
Implement collector types beyond ShellCollector.

Types:
1. DisplayCollector - shows collected text in a panel. No action on trigger, just display.
2. FileCollector - writes collected tokenes to a file on trigger.
3. ConcatCollector - reassembles tokenes back into a string, outputs as single tokene.
4. CounterCollector - counts tokenes absorbed, displays count. 
5. SortCollector - buffers tokenes and sorts them (alphabetically, by size, by encoding) before outputting.

Each collector:
- Has configurable buffer capacity
- Has trigger mode (:on_full | :manual | :on_tick)
- Has optional output chunker (re-chunk the output)
- Has optional output emitter (can chain: collect -> process -> emit)
close_reason: Added 4 new collector actions: Display (passthrough), Reverse, Upcase, Count (chars+bytes). All with UI buttons. 5 new tests.

title: Bug: World GenServer leaks on LiveView disconnect
description: World.start_link creates anonymous unlinked GenServer in mount. On disconnect/crash, the World process becomes an orphan. Fix: Process.link(world_pid) or supervise under DynamicSupervisor.
close_reason: Added Process.link(world_pid) in mount/3. World GenServer now dies when LiveView disconnects.

title: Backend: Collector overflow and perf fixes
description: 1. No capacity guard before absorb - collector overflows. 2. O(n) list append + length per absorption - use prepend + count. 3. get_emit_rate does N GenServer calls per emit - fetch once. 4. fire_all is N+1 round trips - add World.fire_all/1. 5. Broadcast before auto-trigger ordering.
close_reason: Collector capacity guard before absorb. Broadcast moved after auto-trigger. get_emit_rate called once per emit event. Credo unless/else fixed to if/else.

title: Additional Emitter Types
description:
Implement emitter types beyond ShellEmitter.

Types:
1. FileEmitter - reads a file, chunks contents, emits. Good for demos.
2. ClockEmitter - emits formatted time string at configurable interval. Auto-repeating.
3. ManualEmitter - text input field, user types and hits emit. Good for testing.
4. LLMEmitter - streams from an LLM API, natural token boundaries. 
   Uses streaming API, emits tokens as they arrive (real-time feel).
   Could connect to local ollama or OpenAI-compatible API.
5. StdinEmitter - reads from a pipe/stdin (for CLI integration later)

Each emitter:
- Has a configurable chunker (override output chunking)
- Has emit_rate (delay between tokene spawns for visual effect)
- Can be one-shot or auto-repeating

title: Collector Buffer & Absorption
description:
Implement collector buffer mechanics and tokene absorption.

Buffer mechanics:
- Buffer is an ordered array of slots with configurable capacity
- Each slot holds one tokene
- Proximity sensor (Rapier sensor collider) around collector detects nearby tokenes
- When tokene enters sensor zone, client reports to server
- Server decides whether to absorb (buffer has space)
- On absorb: tokene removed from world, added to buffer, client animates

Trigger mechanics:
- :on_full - auto-fires when buffer reaches capacity
- :manual - user clicks trigger button
- :on_tick - fires every N ticks if buffer is non-empty
- On trigger: collector concatenates buffer tokene values, executes its action
  (e.g., ShellCollector runs 'echo <concatenated>')
- Output of trigger can itself be emitted as new tokenes (collector has optional output chunker)

Visual:
- Buffer slots visible as rectangles on/in the collector
- Filled slots show tokene text
- Empty slots are outlined/dimmed
- Fill animation: tokene slides into slot position
close_reason: Core mechanics implemented: Collector.absorb/2 backend, World.absorb_tokene with auto-trigger on full, sensor detection in world_hook.js with cooldown, onAbsorbTokene removes physics body. Buffer slot visuals and advanced trigger modes are future polish.

title: Tokene Rendering
description:
Render tokenes as visual objects in the Three.js scene.

Visual design:
- Rounded rectangles (2D planes with rounded corners)
- Size proportional to byte_size (bits = tiny, sentences = large blocks)
- Text rendered on face showing the tokene value
- Color coding by encoding type or source emitter
- Integrity visualized: high integrity = solid/opaque, low = cracked/translucent
- Spawn animation (pop in from emitter)
- Absorb animation (shrink into buffer slot)
- Split animation (crack apart into smaller pieces)
- Fuse animation (merge together)

Text rendering options:
- Canvas texture (simplest, good for 2D)
- SDF text (crisp at all zoom levels)
- Start with canvas texture

Performance:
- Instance meshes for many tokenes of similar size
- Object pooling for frequently created/destroyed tokenes
- LOD: hide text at far zoom, show colored rect only
close_reason: Implemented in renderer.js: createTokeneMesh with canvas text textures, encoding color map (8 colors), updateTokeneTransform, removeTokene. Rounded rect planes with text on face, color-coded by encoding type.

title: Transformer Nodes Implementation
description:
Implement the transformer node category - active elements that modify tokenes.

Each transformer has a radius/zone of effect (Rapier sensor).

Priority implementations:
1. Splitter - breaks tokene down one encoding level. Uses split hierarchy.
   Rolls against tokene integrity: if random() > integrity, split succeeds.
2. Fuser - when 2+ tokenes are in its zone, combines them into one larger tokene.
   New encoding is one level up from highest input encoding.
3. Heater - reduces integrity of tokenes in zone by configurable rate per tick.
4. Cooler - increases integrity of tokenes in zone.
5. Filter - only lets tokenes matching a regex pattern pass. Blocks others (becomes solid collider for non-matching).

Secondary:
6. Crusher - immediately breaks to bytes (Splitter with force)
7. Retokenizer - re-chunks using a different chunker entirely
8. Painter - assigns color/tag to tokenes
9. Duplicator - spawns a copy of any tokene passing through
10. Spinner - applies angular velocity/torque to tokenes in zone
close_reason: Transformer spawn UI (splitter/heater/cooler/duplicator/crusher buttons), sensor detection in world_hook.js, tokene_near_transformer event handler, transform_tokene push event with new tokene data, effect radius circle visualization in renderer.

title: Investigate: Move physics to backend (Elixir)
description:
Evaluate moving all physics simulation from Rapier2D (client WASM) to the Elixir backend. Frontend would become a pure renderer receiving position/rotation updates via LiveView pushes.

Pros:
- Server-authoritative physics = no cheating, no desync
- Single source of truth for all state
- Simpler client (just Three.js rendering)
- Multiplayer-ready (all clients see same physics)
- No WASM download (3MB saved)

Cons:
- Elixir has no native physics engine (would need to build or port one)
- Higher server CPU (physics per tick per world)
- Network latency for position updates (30-60fps push events)
- Loss of client-side interactivity feel (drag lag)

Options to investigate:
1. Pure Elixir physics: simple gravity + AABB collision (enough for falling rectangles?)
2. Rust NIF wrapping rapier2d (native perf, complex FFI)
3. Port-based: Rapier runs in a Rust sidecar process
4. Hybrid: server owns logic + coarse physics, client does cosmetic physics + interpolation

Research needed:
- Can we get 60fps for 100+ bodies in Elixir without NIFs?
- What physics features do we actually need? (gravity, AABB, sensors, friction)
- LiveView push_event throughput at 30-60fps with 100 body transforms
- Existing Elixir physics libs (if any)

title: Tokene Data Model
description:
Define the Tokene struct and supporting types.

Tokene struct:
- id (unique)
- value (binary - the string content)
- encoding (:bit | :byte | :rune | :token | :ngram | :word | :phrase | :sentence)
- byte_size (determines mass/geometry in physics)
- integrity (0.0-1.0, resistance to splitting)
- source_id (emitter that created it)
- created_at
- metadata (color, stream index, etc)

Integrity defaults by encoding:
  :bit -> 1.0 (atomic, cannot split)
  :byte -> 0.95
  :rune -> 0.8
  :token -> 0.6
  :word -> 0.4
  :phrase -> 0.2
  :sentence -> 0.1

Split hierarchy: sentence -> phrase -> word -> token -> rune -> byte -> bit
When a tokene splits, it re-chunks at the next level down.

Include functions:
- new/3 (value, encoding, source_id)
- split/2 (tokene, target_encoding)
- fuse/2 ([tokenes], new_encoding)
- mass/1 (derive from byte_size)
- dimensions/1 (derive width/height from byte_size)
close_reason: Tokene struct with integrity, mass, dimensions, split hierarchy. Full test suite.

description:
Add Postgres as an alternative/production database backend alongside SQLite.

Currently using SQLite (ecto_sqlite3) for simplicity. When deploying or needing more robust persistence, add Postgres support:
- Add {:postgrex, ">= 0.0.0"} to deps

title: Physics-Logic Bridge (Client-Server Sync)
description:
Implement the communication protocol between client physics and server logic.

Client -> Server events:
- tokene_entered_buffer(tokene_id, collector_id) - proximity sensor triggered
- tokene_entered_zone(tokene_id, transformer_id) - transformer sensor triggered
- tokene_offscreen(tokene_id) - cleanup
- node_moved(node_id, {x, y}) - user dragged node
- node_resized(node_id, {w, h}) - user resized passive element

Server -> Client events (via LiveView push or channel):
- emit_tokenes(emitter_id, [tokene_data]) - spawn physics bodies
- absorb_tokene(collector_id, tokene_id, slot_index) - remove body, animate to slot
- split_tokene(tokene_id, [new_tokene_data]) - remove body, spawn smaller bodies
- fuse_tokenes([tokene_ids], new_tokene_data) - remove bodies, spawn merged body
- trigger_output(collector_id, output_text) - collector fired
- update_node(node_id, changes) - node config changed

Protocol:
- Use Phoenix LiveView hooks + pushEvent/handleEvent
- Or dedicated Phoenix Channel for high-frequency physics events
- Consider: LiveView for UI, Channel for physics (separate concerns)
close_reason: Implemented in world_hook.js: client→server events (tokene_near_collector, tokene_offscreen) and server→client events (emit_tokenes, absorb_tokene, add_node, remove_node, clear_tokenes, set_gravity). Uses LiveView pushEvent/handleEvent with sensor cooldown.

title: Security: Harden shell command execution
description: Shell emitter/collector execute arbitrary commands from WebSocket params. Collector.Shell interpolates unsanitized command into sh -c. Fix: allowlist commands in add_emitter, pass args as argv not shell string, validate snapshot commands.
close_reason: Shell collector uses argv instead of sh -c interpolation. Shell emitter commands allowlisted in LiveView. Snapshot deserialization uses safe allowlist functions.

title: Frontend: Fix memory leaks in renderer disposal
description: 1. dispose() doesn't clean up scene meshes/geometries - GPU leak on navigation. 2. removeTokene() doesn't free texture from cache. 3. Pending setTimeout callbacks from onEmitTokenes not cancelled on destroy.
close_reason: dispose() now cleans up all meshes, node groups, and geometries. Pending setTimeout handles tracked and cleared on destroyed(). onClearNodes properly removes old floor.

title: Frontend: Fix critical physics and rendering bugs
description: 1. Sensor removal broken - use-after-free in Rapier (attach sensor to existing body instead of separate fixed body). 2. setGravity assigns plain object, needs rapier.Vector2. 3. Map mutation during animate() iteration. 4. onClearNodes leaks floor bodies. 5. setTimeout fires after destroyed().
close_reason: Sensor attached to existing kinematic body (follows node). setGravity uses rapier.Vector2. Animate loop collects offscreen IDs before mutating. onClearNodes removes floor before re-adding. remove() cleans up sensor bodies. onRemoveNode cleans up sensorCooldown.
